verdict: OK to lend in Alappuzha shrimp processing — back established processors with US/EU order books and cold-chain discipline; avoid single-buyer, thin-margin units and any proposal riding on the harbour upgrade alone.
title: Alappuzha seafood / shrimp processing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A shrimp processor buys raw shrimp from peeling sheds and landing centres, freezes it, and sells containers to US, EU and now non-US buyers — cash turns on the cold chain, not the plant.** Value sits in the freezer and in the buyer relationship; the plant is mostly blast freezers, IQF lines and cold storage, so capex is modest and repeatable. Pricing power is thin: the exporter is a price-taker against Ecuador and Vietnam, and margin comes from raw-material timing and realisation, not from brand. **So when a proposal lands, check the buyer list and the realisation per kg first; if one buyer is above half of sales, ask for the offtake contract and the last twelve months of shipping bills.**

## Where cash actually sits
**Working capital is the whole business: raw shrimp is paid for in days, the container is paid for in weeks, and the freezer carries the gap.** Peer evidence shows how tight this is — one rated processor ran maximum working-capital utilisation at about 96% for the twelve months to June 30, 2025 and took a temporary overdraft from existing lenders [8]. **So size the drawing power on stock-and-debtor, not on turnover; if the customer asks for a limit above what the book supports, ask for the stock statement and the age of receivables.** Margins are moving the right way at the listed end: Apex Frozen Foods lifted EBITDA margin to 12.7% from 7.1% and PAT 138% year-on-year on a 15% rise in average realisation, with flat revenue [3][4].

## What has changed now
**The rating view has flipped from flat to growth: CRISIL now expects India's shrimp exports to cross Rs 50,000 crore this fiscal, up 13-15% on-year after three years of stagnation, as exporters shift to markets other than the US [7].** That is a March 2026 rating report and the earlier May 2025 report had volumes flat on US tariffs [6] — treat the older one as history. Peer results are current and confirm demand: Avanti's Q2 FY26 gross income was up 18.75% year-on-year with strong shrimp processing and export volumes [2], and shrimp stocks rallied in April 2026 on easing US tariffs [5]. Locally, the only Alappuzha item is a political statement that Valiyazheekkal fishing harbour development will be completed on time, with Rs 16.67 crore of works done under the Nabard scheme [1]. **That is a landing-side convenience, not a demand signal — so do not let a harbour-linked proposal borrow against it; ask what the unit's own buyer book looks like.**

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue established processors with a diversified buyer mix, own cold storage, and a peeling-shed supply chain they control; avoid traders who only aggregate and any unit whose sales depend on a single overseas importer.** The Sandhya Aqua rating shows the pattern to test: one promoter-group buyer took about 25% of that company's requirements, which is growth potential but also concentration [9]. Structure as cash credit against stock and receivables plus a term loan only for freezer capacity, with a monthly stock-and-debtor statement, a covenant capping single-buyer share, and a check that the temporary overdraft is not being rolled. **Take every month: stock statement, debtor ageing, shipping bills, and the realised price per kg — if realisation falls while volumes rise, ask why before renewing.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the freezer, not the P&L: rising stock days with flat sales means the buyer has slowed and the raw material is ageing.** Watch buyer concentration and any shift of sales to a new, unrated importer. Watch drawing power utilisation sitting near the ceiling month after month, as at the rated peer [8].
watch: Stock days rise while sales are flat -> ask for buyer-wise sales register and hold renewal
Single buyer above half of sales -> require offtake contract or cap exposure
Realisation per kg from shipping bills (monthly)
Realisation falls while volumes rise -> ask why before renewing limit
Any fresh TOD from another lender -> treat as stress and review account
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
news_why: Rating upgrade to 13-15% export growth and strong peer margins outweigh flat-volume history.
